title: Private Connect Gateway: deterministic handshake, offline validation, and upgrade safety acceptance
creator: Ava Carter
description:
Purpose: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for the Private Connect Gateway feature — a light-weight, deterministic connection handshake and artifact validation path used by Private/VPC deployments during bootstrap, upgrades, and graceful fallback. This ticket captures the PRD-level constraints for networking, air-gapped operation, and upgrade safety.

Scope:
- Provide a minimal outbound connection protocol (Connect Gateway) for operator-controlled artifact pulls and health probes with deterministic behavior across isolated networks.
- Offer an offline validation mode that supports signed artifact verification and checksum reconciliation without relying on full egress.
- Define staged upgrade compatibility matrix for operator agents (operator-connector, kernel interaction, container runtime) to prevent post-upgrade partitioning.

Out of scope for this ticket (moved to separate follow-ups): image-signing implementation (will be tracked in PM-777002), and UI console rollout controls (tracked under console-2025.03).
requirements: REQ-01: Connect Gateway must support a deterministic 3-step handshake (SYN / AUTH / ACK) that succeeds or fails within a 10s timeout when trying to reach a configured mirror or proxy endpoint.
REQ-02: Handshake must be resilient to transient DNS resolution failures and include an optional pre-configured IP fallback list for air-gapped sites.

REQ-03: All artifact transfers used by upgrades must be accompanied by a signed manifest (detached signature) and SHA-256 checksum; agent must reject artifacts with mismatched checksums when offline-validation is enabled.
REQ-04: Support for two bootstrap modes: online-mirror (minimal egress allowed) and sealed-airgap (no egress; artifacts provided via operator mirror or physical media).

REQ-05: Upgrade orchestration must consult a local compatibility matrix before applying a control-plane image; if matrix indicates incompatibility, system must halt and emit a clear operator action with rollback instructions.

REQ-06: Connect Gateway configuration must be expressible via the private deploy operator CRD and have a single source-of-truth manifest that can be audited for network allowlists and mirror endpoints.
REQ-07: Telemetry disclosures: when operating in online-mirror mode, only minimal metadata (agent version, manifest ID, and success/failure codes) are emitted; no customer payload is sent externally.
REQ-08: RBAC for operator actions: only an authorized operator principal (KMS-backed token or signed operator key) can approve canary-to-wide rollouts during upgrades.

REQ-09: The solution must include an automated simulation harness (controlled chaos) that emulates DNS partitions, mirror lag, and partial artifact corruption to validate rollback and k-safety behaviors.
REQ-10: Provide machine-readable runbook artifacts (YAML) for operator intervention steps and an optional human-friendly PDF for audited customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Deterministic handshake test: in CI, 1000 simulated handshakes across varying latency distributions must have median < 250ms and 99th percentile < 9.5s with clear failure codes when mirror unreachable.

AC-02: Offline validation: when offline-validation mode is set to true, agent rejects any artifact whose SHA-256 does not match the manifest and emits a signed rejection event to the local log for audits.

AC-03: Compatibility matrix enforcement: in an upgrade dry-run, control-plane agent refuses to proceed if any node reports 'compatibility: false' in the matrix and produces a roll-forward plan with required preconditions.

AC-04: Airgap bootstrap scenario: documented end-to-end playbook validated in a representative customer environment (staged test lab) where no egress is permitted; bootstrap succeeds via operator mirror and artifacts pass checksum validation.
AC-05: Minimal telemetry: verification that only allowed telemetry fields are emitted in online-mirror tests (audit script runs and compares outgoing payloads against approved schema).

AC-06: Operator authorization: an attempt to approve a rollout without a valid operator principal is rejected by the control-plane and logged as an access denied event (end-to-end test using mock KMS).

AC-07: Rollback behavior: injected artifact corruption during a canary upgrade triggers automatic pause and a documented rollback path; rollback completes to pre-upgrade state within the SLO (configurable, default 15 minutes).
AC-08: Runbook existence: YAML runbook artifacts are stored in the operator-config repo and linked in the console; audit confirms presence and SHA-256 checksum of the runbook.
test_plan: TP-01: CI integration: add handshake unit tests and deterministic-latency harness; run in nightly pipeline against ubuntu:22.04 and rhel-8 matrix.
TP-02: Staged lab validation: customer-mirror simulation with 3 regional stalls, validate offline bootstrap and operator intervention steps; record video and artifacts for audit.
TP-03: Chaos harness: run 500 randomized partition experiments; ensure that the system either completes bootstrap or emits an operator play with exact remediation steps.
TP-04: Security validation: pen-test of operator token approval flow and replay attacks on handshake (mitigations: nonce + expiry).
TP-05: Performance smoke: measure median connect time and handshake success thresholds in an environment with packet loss up to 3%.
decisions_and_scope_changes: 2025-01-20: Decision: split image-signing work into PM-777002 to unblock handshake and offline validation delivery. Reason: signing implementation requires new key management integration and will delay rollout.
2025-01-28: Scope change: added deterministic handshake timeout strategy (three configurable timeouts) after infra raised issues with flaky DNS during staging tests.
2025-01-31: Decision: use detached manifest signatures (rather than embedded) to simplify airgap verification and keep agent footprint small.
2025-02-02: Clarification: telemetry fields trimmed to approved schema; any future telemetry must go through a privacy review and be opt-in per customer manifest.
Pending: review whether operator-run physical-media ingestion requires a signed chain-of-custody artifact (security wants it; ops prefers a lighter checklist).
